summary: 500-hour service: hydraulic oil sampled, pump pressure 3,150 psi, within spec
detail: Oil sample sent to lab. Pressure test at full RPM read 3,150 psi against a 3,000-3,300 spec. No weeping at the case drain.

summary: Oil sample came back with elevated silicon, flagged to watch for dirt ingress
detail: Lab report: silicon 22 ppm (baseline 8). Suggests dust getting past a breather or seal. No action yet, re-sample at next service.

summary: Daily walkaround, no issues
Operator reports boom feels slow to lift when cold in the mornings
detail: Takes a few minutes of warm-up before the boom lifts at normal speed. Fine once the machine is warm. Didn't notice any leaks.

summary: 1,000-hour service: pressure still in spec, light oil film found on pump housing
detail: Pressure 3,080 psi. Wiped a light film off the housing near the drive-end seal. Cleaned and marked with chalk to see if it comes back. Oil re-sampled.

summary: Fresh hydraulic oil found pooling under the right access panel during walkaround
detail: About a palm-sized puddle on the belly pan under the pump. Oil looks clean, not burnt. Machine still runs normally. Tagged for the shop.

summary: Replaced pump drive-end shaft seal and case drain O-ring, leak stopped
detail: Seal lip was hardened and grooved. Case drain O-ring also flattened. Replaced both, topped off 2 liters of oil, ran 20 minutes at temp with no weep. Root cause likely the dust ingress flagged last spring; recommend checking the tank breather.

summary: Follow-up check one week after seal replacement, housing dry
detail: Chalk mark intact, no new film. Pressure 3,120 psi.

summary: Faint film reappearing at the drive-end seal, far earlier than expected
detail: Spotted a thin wet ring at the seal during the walkaround, about 3 months after the replacement. Not dripping. Hours since repair: roughly 400. Could be the same contamination issue; the breather still hasn't been checked.

summary: Rod and gland checked at 500-hour service, no scoring, no leaks
Boom drifts down about 2 inches over 10 minutes when parked with the bucket raised
detail: Noticed during lunch break with the bucket held up. Slow steady drift, no visible leaks on the rod.

summary: Resealed boom cylinder piston, drift test now passes
detail: Internal bypass across the piston seal. Replaced the seal kit, checked the bore for scoring (none). Drift under 1/4 inch over 10 minutes after repair.

summary: Daily walkaround, rod clean, no drift noticed
Primary air filter replaced at 500-hour service
detail: Restriction indicator was in the yellow. Secondary filter inspected, left in place.

summary: Filter clogging faster than usual on the dusty north pit, restriction indicator tripping early
detail: Hit the red on the indicator about 300 hours after the last change. Blew it out with shop air to finish the week. Site is very dusty this summer.

summary: Primary and secondary air filters replaced, interval shortened to 250 hours for this site
detail: Both filters heavy with fine dust. Shop-air cleaning had torn a pleat on the primary. Reset indicator. Told the operator not to blow filters out again, replace instead.

summary: Restriction indicator checked at walkaround, in the green
Track tension measured and adjusted, sag was 2 inches over spec
detail: Grease added at the adjuster to bring sag back to spec. Sprocket teeth starting to hook, roughly 50 percent worn.

summary: Left final drive weeping gear oil at the sprocket hub
detail: Dark oil streak down the inside of the sprocket after a shift. Not a drip yet.

summary: Replaced left final drive floating seal (duo-cone), refilled gear oil
detail: Seal face had a small chip from a trapped rock. Drained and refilled 4.5 liters of 80W-90. No metal on the magnetic plug.

summary: Brake pad wear warning on the dash at 17,900 miles, earlier than expected
detail: Yellow brake pad symbol came on during the commute. No noise, pedal feels normal. Dealer said front pads usually go 25 to 30k on this car.

summary: Front pads measured: left inner 2 mm, left outer 6 mm, right side even at 5 mm
detail: Only the left front is wearing unevenly. Pulled the caliper. Both guide pins were dry and the lower one was stiff in its bore, so the inner pad was dragging. Rotors within spec, 30.2 mm against a 28.4 minimum.

summary: Front pads and wear sensor replaced, left caliper guide pins cleaned and greased
detail: New pads and a new wear sensor on the left front. Cleaned both guide pins, new boots, high-temp brake grease. Rotors kept. Bedded the pads over ten stops from 60. Service reminder reset.

summary: Tire rotation check, front pads even at 8 mm both sides
detail: Measured through the spokes with a gauge. Left inner and outer within 0.5 mm of each other. Pins are doing their job.

summary: Annual inspection, pads at 6 mm, rotors clean, fluid tested at 2 percent moisture
detail: Brake fluid due for a flush next spring under the two-year schedule. No pulsation on a hard stop from 70.

summary: Faint squeal from the left front on the first cold stop each morning, gone after that
detail: Started about a week ago. Only the first stop of the day and only turning right, which loads the left front. Pedal feels fine, no warning light.

summary: Tire rotation and tread check, inner shoulder on the front tires wearing faster
detail: Front inner edge 4/32, outer edge 6/32 on both fronts. Normal for the factory camber on this car but worth rotating on time. Pressures set to 35 psi cold all around.

summary: Low tire pressure warning, left front down to 27 psi
detail: Warning came on overnight in the driveway. Other three tires at 34 to 35. Found a drywall screw in the center of the tread.

summary: Screw removed, tire patched from the inside, wheel rebalanced
detail: Puncture was in the center tread, repairable. Plug-patch applied from the inside. Rebalanced. Tread 5/32 inner, 6/32 outer. TPMS relearned.

summary: Pressure holding at 35 psi four months after the patch
Oil and filter changed at 32,100 miles, 0W-30 full synthetic
detail: Drained hot, 6.9 quarts in. New filter and drain plug washer. Service reminder reset. No metal on the plug.

summary: Low oil level message on the dash, added one quart
detail: The car has no dipstick, so I checked the level on the screen after idling. It showed one bar under MIN. Added a quart of the same 0W-30 and the level read in the middle of the range.

summary: Oil consumption is one quart per 4,000 miles, within what the factory calls normal for this engine
detail: Checked under the car and around the oil filter housing and valve cover, all dry. No blue smoke on a cold start. Keep a quart of 0W-30 in the trunk and check the level on the screen every other fuel stop.

summary: Engine air filter replaced at 30,000 miles
detail: Old filter was gray with leaves and a few seed pods in the airbox. Vacuumed the box before fitting the new filter.

summary: Dust found on the clean side of the airbox, rear clip had not been seated
detail: Opened the box during the annual inspection and saw a thin line of dust past the filter seal. The rear clip on the lid was sitting on top of its catch instead of under it. Cleaned the box, seated the filter, and pressed all clips until they clicked. Filter itself still fine.

summary: Slow crank on cold mornings, starts on the second try below freezing
detail: Fine once it is running and fine the rest of the day. Noticed it twice this week.

summary: Battery tested at 12.4 volts resting, 520 of 800 rated cold cranking amps, five years old
detail: AGM battery in the trunk under the floor panel. Passed the load test with little margin. Terminals clean. On this car a replacement has to be registered to the car with a scan tool or it will be overcharged. Plan to replace before next winter.
